---
title: "Chunk options"
---

## Introduction

Chunk options control how a chunk's code is executed and how its results appear in the rendered document — whether the
code is shown, whether messages are printed, how figures are sized, and more.

::: {.column-margin}
::: resource
[Quarto documentation on chunk options](https://quarto.org/docs/computations/r.html#chunk-options)
:::
:::

Quarto specifies chunk options as commented lines beginning with `#|`, directly below the chunk header, rather than
inline in the curly braces:

````markdown
#| label: data-summary
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
````

## Display Control: `echo`

The `echo` option controls whether the chunk's source code itself appears in the rendered document; the result is
always shown regardless. 

**Predict:** given the chunk below sets `echo: FALSE`, will the rendered document show the
code, the result, both, or neither?

````markdown
#| echo: FALSE
mean(c(5, 10, 15))
````

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
mean(c(5, 10, 15))
```

**Explain:** as shown above, only the result (10) appears; the `mean(c(5, 10, 15))` code itself is hidden. `results`,
`warning`, and `message` work the same way for their respective content: each independently controls whether that one
type of output is shown, without affecting whether the code or other outputs appear.

::: {.callout-note}
## Common Mistake

`echo: FALSE` and `include: FALSE` are easy to confuse. `echo: FALSE` hides only the code, while the result (text,
table, or plot) still appears. `include: FALSE` hides both code and result while still running the chunk.
Use `include: FALSE` for setup chunks (like loading packages) that should run silently, and `echo: FALSE` when you want
the reader to see a result without the code that produced it.
:::

## Execution Options

* **`eval`** determines whether the chunk is executed at all (`TRUE`/`FALSE`).
* **`error`** determines whether rendering continues if the chunk throws an error (`TRUE`) or stops (`FALSE`).

A setup chunk that loads packages but shouldn't appear in the final report combines these ideas:

````markdown
#| label: setup
#| include: FALSE

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
````

## Figure and Table Options

When a chunk produces a plot or table, these options control its appearance:

* **`fig-cap`** adds a caption.
* **`fig-width`** / **`fig-height`** set the dimensions, in inches.
* **`fig-align`** sets the alignment (`"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`).

````markdown
#| label: visualization
#| echo: FALSE
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of scores by group."
````

## Caching

Setting **`cache: TRUE`** saves a chunk's results so they don't need to be recomputed on every render, unless the code
itself changes. This is useful for slow computations in large documents, but remember to clear the cache if the
underlying data changes without the code changing.

::: practice

## Practice Exercise

:::: {.panel-tabset}
## {{< var tab_title.question >}}

You want a chunk's plot to appear in the rendered report, captioned "Figure 1: Distribution of scores," but without
showing the ggplot code that created it. Which two chunk options do you need, and what would you set them to?

## {{< var tab_title.solution >}}

`echo: FALSE` to hide the code while keeping the plot, and `fig-cap: "Figure 1: Distribution of scores"` to add the
caption.

::::

:::
